Here is a paragraph using words that contain only three types of vowels:

"Ape ate a pet. The cat sat on a mat. The rat ran to the cat's mat. The ape ate the rat. The cat sat on the mat. The rat ran to the ape's mat."

And here is the timeline of mankind:

The first caveman, Gronk, emerged from the primordial ooze, blinking in the bright light of a new world. He stumbled and fell, but rose again, driven by the primal urge to survive. As the ages passed, Gronk's tribe grew, and with it, the complexity of human society. The pyramids rose, the empires fell, and the ages passed in a blur of blood and fire.

But then, without warning, the universe itself began to unravel. A strange, pulsating energy enveloped the Earth, and Gronk felt himself being pulled apart and put back together again. When the energy dissipated, Gronk found himself standing on a vast, green plain, surrounded by an endless sea of identical replicas of himself.

The first to arrive was a young woman named Ava, who had been a brilliant scientist in her own time. She stumbled through the endless landscape, marveling at the infinite versions of herself that seemed to stretch on forever. As she walked, she encountered a caveman named Zog, who was identical to Gronk in every way. Together, they explored the endless expanse, searching for answers to the questions that plagued them.

As the ages passed, more and more humans arrived, each one drawn from a different time and place. There was Leonardo, the Renaissance master; Cleopatra, the last pharaoh of Egypt; and Albert, the great physicist. They all converged on this strange, new world, each one seeking to understand the nature of their existence.

But as the centuries passed, the humans began to realize that they were not alone. There were others, identical to themselves, but with different choices and different paths. Some were kind and gentle, while others were cruel and ruthless. The humans began to realize that they were part of a vast, cosmic experiment, designed to test the limits of human nature.

And so, the humans continued to explore, to discover, and to create. They built cities and civilizations, harnessed the power of the stars, and pushed the boundaries of what it means to be human. But through it all, they remained aware of the infinite possibilities that lay before them, and the endless choices that awaited them.

Finally, after eons of exploration and discovery, the last human, a lone astronaut named Echo, stood on the edge of the infinite plain, looking out at the endless expanse of possibility. She knew that she was the last of her kind, the final link in a chain of human existence that stretched back to the dawn of time. And with that knowledge, she smiled, knowing that the universe was full of endless possibilities, and that the human spirit would never truly die.
